name: Québec
note: In Quebec a physician or nurse (or two peace officers) draws up the constat de décès, and the spouse or a relative declares the death without delay to the Directeur de l'état civil, the province's single civil-status officer, usually signing it with the funeral company. The DEC draws up the act of death. The medical bulletin reaches the Health Ministry and the statistics institute within three days, increasingly electronically through SIED. If the family also signs a simplified-transmission request, the DEC tells RAMQ, Retraite Québec, social assistance, Revenu Québec, the CRA and Service Canada in one step. RAMQ passes dates of death to the electoral list. Certificates are restricted to persons with an interest.

steps.title: Physician or nurse draws up the constat de décès
steps.who: A physician, or since 7 June 2023 any nurse (specialized nurse practitioner or not). If neither can attend within a reasonable time and death is obvious, two peace officers.
steps.summary: Whoever finds the death draws up the constat de décès and gives one copy to the person who must declare the death. Two peace officers may do so when no physician or nurse can attend in reasonable time and death is obvious. A nurse other than an IPS who cannot establish the probable causes must notify a physician or IPS.

steps.title: Constat sent to the Directeur de l'état civil
steps.who: The physician or nurse, or the funeral services company that takes charge of the body.
steps.summary: A second copy of the constat goes without delay to the Directeur de l'état civil, normally together with the declaration of death. The constat (DEC-101) is a carbon copy of the medical bulletin (SP-3), and the electronic SIED system can send it to the DEC directly.

steps.title: Physician or nurse practitioner notifies the coroner
steps.who: The physician or IPS who cannot establish the probable causes, or for whom the death appears due to negligence or obscure or violent circumstances. Anyone may report a death they think escaped the coroner.
steps.trigger: Unknown cause; violent, obscure or negligent death.
steps.summary: Deaths of unknown cause, or that seem violent, obscure or negligent, must be reported immediately to a coroner or a peace officer. The coroner's office gives the family an attestation of death within 24 to 48 hours. It serves some administrative steps but cannot be used to enter the death in the civil register.

steps.title: Certifier sends the bulletin de décès (SP-3) to the Ministry of Health
steps.who: The physician, IPS or nurse who certifies the death, using the SP-3 form or the electronic SIED; not the coroner.

deadline.text: within three days after the death

steps.summary: The medical cause of death goes on the bulletin de décès, which public-health regulation requires to reach the Minister of Health within three days. Through SIED the same data go to the Institut de la statistique du Québec and the DEC.

steps.title: Relative declares the death to the Directeur de l'état civil
steps.who: The spouse, a close relative or relative by marriage, or failing them anyone able to identify the deceased; signed in the presence of the funeral services company, which adds the time, place and mode of disposal.
steps.summary: Quebec has a single civil-status officer, the Directeur de l'état civil. The declaration of death goes to it without delay from the spouse or a relative. When a funeral company takes charge of the body, it declares how and where the body was disposed of. The family signs the declaration with the funeral company's representative.

steps.title: Directeur de l'état civil draws up the act of death
steps.trigger: Receipt of the constat and the declaration.
steps.summary: The DEC draws up the acte de décès without delay from the constat and declaration it receives, by signing the declaration, after a summary inquiry if needed.

steps.title: Funeral company may move the body only with the constat
steps.who: The funeral services company or its contracted carrier.
steps.summary: In Quebec it is the constat de décès, not the registration, that the funeral sector needs. A carrier must hold the constat (accessible in SIED) to transport a body. Moving a body out of Quebec requires a coroner's authorization.

steps.title: DEC issues copies of the act and death certificates
steps.localName: certificat de décès / copie d'acte de décès
steps.who: Only the persons named in the act, or persons who show an interest (the liquidator, heirs); the funeral company may apply online for the family.
steps.trigger: Application (the family or liquidator applies separately from the declaration).
steps.summary: The register is made public only through copies, certificates and attestations issued by the DEC. These go only to the persons named in the act or to those who show an interest, and the register cannot be consulted without the DEC's authorization. The liquidator needs these documents for the succession.

steps.title: DEC notifies ministries and agencies (simplified transmission)
steps.who: The Directeur de l'état civil, if the family completed the 'Demande de transmission simplifiée de renseignements relatifs au décès' with the funeral company.
steps.trigger: Registration, when the simplified-transmission request was made.
steps.summary: Quebec runs a tell-once service. If the family signs the simplified-transmission request with the declaration, the DEC informs RAMQ, Retraite Québec (QPP and family allowance), the Ministry of Employment and Social Solidarity, Revenu Québec, the CRA and Service Canada (Social Insurance Register). On request it can also inform others, such as the SAAQ, CNESST, firearms registries and Indigenous Services Canada. Otherwise the family must notify each body.

steps.title: DEC notifies Service Canada's Social Insurance Register and the CRA
steps.who: The Directeur de l'état civil (see ca-federal).
steps.summary: Among the bodies the DEC informs are Service Canada, to update the Social Insurance Register, and the Canada Revenue Agency.

steps.title: Family returns the health insurance card to RAMQ
steps.who: The family; for a death in Quebec the card can be handed to the funeral director.
steps.summary: The family must still inform RAMQ and return the health card, though the funeral director can take it. RAMQ is also on the DEC's automatic list when the simplified request is made. Cancelling the card also ends public drug-insurance registration.

steps.title: RAMQ supplies dates of death to the Chief Electoral Officer
steps.who: The Régie de l'assurance maladie du Québec, to the Directeur général des élections.
steps.trigger: A date of death recorded at RAMQ for a person on the permanent list.
steps.summary: The Directeur général des élections gets changes for listed electors from RAMQ, including the date of death. It removes from the permanent list any person for whom it receives confirmation of death.

steps.title: Death data reach the Institut de la statistique du Québec
steps.who: SIED, from the certifier's electronic bulletin.
steps.summary: The bulletin data are sent electronically to the Institut de la statistique du Québec, which records all demographic events for Quebecers.

steps.title: Liquidator publishes closure of the inventory in the RDPRM
steps.summary: The closure of the inventory is published by registering a notice in the Register of Personal and Movable Real Rights (RDPRM). The notice identifies the deceased and says where interested persons can consult the inventory. This is the public signal to creditors and others.

registrationDeadlineDays.note: Both the constat and the declaration go to the DEC 'sans délai' (without delay); no day count is set. Recorded as 0 to mean immediately.

informantDuty.note: The spouse, a close relative or relative by marriage, or failing them anyone able to identify the deceased. The funeral company adds the disposal details and in practice transmits the declaration.

medicalExaminerScrutiny.note: No independent review of certifiers' bulletins; coroner involvement depends on the duty to notify.

electronicRegistration.note: SIED lets certifiers file the bulletin de décès electronically and passes it to the Ministry, the ISQ and the DEC. Paper SP-3/DEC-101 forms remain in use, and the rollout is still spreading.

centralPopulationRegister.note: The civil register held by the single officer of civil status (DEC) is not a population register that other bodies read from. Onward notification is by DEC transmission.

governmentPropagation.note: If the family signs the simplified-transmission request with the funeral company, the DEC informs RAMQ, Retraite Québec, MESS, Revenu Québec, the CRA and Service Canada. Without it, the family must tell each body.

certificateAccess.note: Copies and certificates go only to persons named in the act or those who show an interest.

privateSectorVerification.note: The register cannot be consulted without the DEC's authorization, and certificates go only to persons with an interest. No death-data service for banks or insurers was found. The public signal for creditors is the liquidator's RDPRM inventory notice.

gaps: The Loi sur la recherche des causes et des circonstances des décès (RLRQ c. R-0.2) could not be read. LégisQuébec returns only the table of regulations for that act in both languages, the PDF route answers 403, and CanLII answers 403. The coroner-notification duty is sourced to the Health Ministry's bulletin page instead, and the R-0.2 citation carries no quote.

www.etatcivil.gouv.qc.ca (Directeur de l'état civil) is blocked by the egress policy (CONNECT 403), so the DEC's own page on 'transmission simplifiée' could not be read. The list used here is from Québec.ca.
The legal basis of the DEC's onward transmissions (exchange agreements under the Act respecting access to documents held by public bodies, or a regulation under CCQ art. 151) was not identified.
The Règlement ministériel d'application de la Loi sur la santé publique (RLRQ c. S-2.2, r. 2.1) three-day bulletin rule is sourced to the Ministry's page, not the regulation text.

The Loi sur les activités funéraires (RLRQ c. A-5.02) and its regulation were not read directly. The constat requirement for transport comes from the Ministry page, and any disposal waiting period was not checked.
Retraite Québec's and RAMQ's own statutory provisions for receiving death data from the DEC were not found in the RRQ Act (R-9) or the Health Insurance Act (A-29).
Quebec has no fixed registration day count ('sans délai'). registrationDeadlineDays is recorded as 0 to mean 'immediately', which may need reinterpretation.
